Every candidate is placed on the same line of sight, at the same elevation above the skyline and the same angular size, because those three things are what the witnesses reported (C09, C55, C18). What differs is how far away each would have to be, how big it is, how it would move, sound and look, and what the group would have seen after the glance away. 'fit' candidates take their size from the angle at a chosen distance; 'fixed' candidates have a known size, so the angle fixes their distance.

page.intro: Five soldiers at the top of a flight of stairs on Fort Carson saw a still, white, panel-textured ellipsoid over Cheyenne Mountain in late morning, glanced at each other, and it was gone. Pick a candidate on the right. Each one is placed exactly where it would have to be to look the way the witnesses said: same direction, same height above the ridge, same size against a thumb at arm's length. Then play the event and see what each would have looked like, how it would have moved, and what would still be in the sky when they looked back.

tiles.txt: The half-thumb gesture at 6 mi means {{size.consistency.gesture_ft_at_6mi|0}} ft; "hundreds of feet" tops out near 900. They agree only within {{size.consistency.dist_mi_for_900|1}} mi.
Beyond this, binocular depth gives nothing. At the pin the disparity is {{stereo.disparity_at_pin_arcsec|1}} arcsec, {{stereo.threshold_over_disparity|0}} times below threshold.
Centre {{obj.default.alt_center_ft|0}} ft MSL. As a gas envelope it would hold {{prop.volume_over_big60|1}} times NASA's largest balloon.
